To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a sesquiterpenoid dialdehyde from a Madagascar tree bark, Cinnamosma, is toxic, antifedant, and repellant to the yellow fever and Zika mosquito, and that this bioactivity requires the mosquito’s TRPA1 ion channel.

the medicinal plant C. fragrans produces a sesquiterpenoid dialdehyde, cinnamodial, that is toxic and antifeedant against the yellow fever mosquito, A. aegyti, and that this molecule acts as an agonist of the mosquito TRPA1 channel.

a bark extract and its major drimeane sesquiterpens from the Malagasy medicinal plant, Cinnamosma frangrans, are insecticidal and antifeedant to Aedes aeygpti, and these bioactivities are dependent upon the mosquito transient receptor potential A1 (TRAPA1) channel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery and characterization of natural products that are toxic to mosquito vectors of human pathogens.
the discovery and characterization of a novel mosquito repellent and insecticide derived from the Madagascar plant Cinnamosoma fragrans.
the discovery of novel natural insecticides from plants.

we have discovered a natural product that is toxic, and repellent, to the yellow fever and Zika virus vector, the mosquito Aedes aegispti.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a natural product isolated from the bark of C. fragrans is toxic, antifedant and repellents to Aedes aepyti, the principal mosquito that transmits yellow fever, Zika, dengue and chikungunya viruses.
the bark of Cinnamosoma fragrans is a potential source of natural products with insecticidal, repellent, and antifeedant properties that may be useful for controlling mosquito vectors.
